A1.justification: Despite the changed title, both PDFs describe the same composite-priority Treap/B-Treap research. Text, equations and figures support reliable comparison, including the earlier analyses redistributed into v3's appendices.

before.justification: v2 reports theoretical results, proofs and illustrative access sequences, followed by references. It contains no original experimental, simulation or data-analysis outcomes.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendix E report original synthetic experiments comparing access costs across data structures, distributions and prediction-error conditions.

M1.justification: The core construction remains, and v3's working-set score matches v2's interval-set score after renaming. Limited procedural revisions include changing B-tree bucketing from log_4 to log_2 in Theorems 3.1/C.2 and replacing the stated 11-wise hash construction with independent uniform offsets for BSTs. Some dynamic appendix formulas still retain log_4.

E1.justification: v2 has no empirical evaluation coverage. v3 evaluates synthetic access sequences from Zipfian, adversarial and uniform distributions, including inaccurate frequency predictions and adversarial/Zipfian or adversarial/uniform mixtures. These are newly evaluated scenarios, although some distributions already appeared in v2's theoretical arguments.

E2.justification: Figures 2–5 introduce evaluated comparisons against Lin–Luo–Woodruff's learned BST, Fu et al.'s learned skip-list, red-black trees, AVL trees, splay trees, order-3 B-trees and randomized Treaps. Appendix E compares against splay trees and randomized Treaps. v2's theoretical comparisons do not constitute these empirical evaluations.

E3.justification: v3 introduces randomized insertion order, comparison counts as access cost, and stated settings of n=1000 with m ranging from 2000 to 20000. Prediction-error experiments use n=5000, m=10000 and controlled KL divergence. These are new protocols; the prose incorrectly calls the horizontal axis unique items where Figures 2–4 and 8 label it accesses.

E4.justification: Sections 5.2–5.3 add empirical tests of degradation with prediction error and the relationship between cost and KL divergence. Appendix E adds distribution-mismatch tests with 25%, 50% and 75% Zipfian or uniform mixing. v2 contains theoretical robustness analysis but no corresponding empirical sensitivity tests.

E5.justification: v3 states that all experimental results use ten independent trials and displays error bars; v2 has no empirical uncertainty reporting. This is a limited reporting addition: the PDFs do not identify the bars as standard deviations, standard errors or confidence intervals, and v3 supplies no seed values.

E6.justification: All experimental results in Figures 2–6 and 8 are new. Figures 2–4 show learn-bst behind learn-llw on Zipfian data but with the lowest plotted costs on adversarial and uniform data. Further results show increasing costs with KL divergence and favorable mixture performance against splay trees and randomized Treaps. These are newly reported results, not performance improvements over v2 experiments.

T1.justification: v2 Theorem 6.9 bounds dynamic noise overhead using raw-score error and O(m log_B(1+nε/m)); v3 Theorems 4.5/D.9 instead use summed absolute log-score errors with explicit conditions on locally changing predictions. Appendix D adds general local-score guarantees and revises the general prediction-error bound. v3 also corrects the weight substitution in the static robustness proof from 1/q_x to q_x and removes v2's stated minimum-frequency assumption from the static robustness discussion.

C1.justification: v3 adds empirical superiority over prior and classical data structures as an abstract-level contribution and changes the advertised dynamic robustness guarantee to log-score error. It drops v2's claims of the first B-tree with access-sequence-dependent bounds and bounds unknown to existing BSTs. The central static-optimality and working-set claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4 newly discusses the future information required by the working-set score and suggests past-only proxies or learned predictors as practical approximations. Appendix D motivates predicting log-scores to capture their scale. v3 also interprets its new KL and mixture experiments as robustness evidence; the existing temporal-locality and update-cost discussion largely remains.

D1.justification: v3 adds implementation information for synthetic experiments, notably constructing controlled-KL predictions with SciPy's SLSQP optimizer initialized from a uniform distribution. This modestly improves reproducibility documentation. Neither PDF provides a code-release link, and v3 does not supply detailed implementation versions or hardware information.

R1.justification: v3 adds Bose et al. (2008) on self-adjusting B-trees, Greedy BST references, Fu et al. (2025), and session-recommendation context. It also gives more precise Tango-tree positioning and removes the earlier broad first-B-tree assertions. Most related-work discussion is retained, largely in Appendix A, rather than replaced.

P1.justification: v3 substantially rewrites the abstract and introduction, adds explicit research questions and a contribution list, and reorganizes overview and related work into introductory subsections. Extensive theoretical material moves into Appendices A–D, with experiments in Section 5 and Appendix E. The title, author listing and interval-set/working-set terminology also change.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes a two-column main paper with single-column appendices. v3 adds Figures 2–6 and the six-panel Figure 8, rearranges Figure 1, and relocates/relabels v2 Figure 2 as Figure 7. Figure 7's caption retains the old work/interval terminology despite the diagram's revised labels.

improvement.justification: v3 adds useful empirical evidence about comparative performance and prediction-error robustness, corrects the static robustness proof's weight substitution, and clarifies local-update guarantees. These improve assessment of the largely retained construction. The net gain is limited by undefined error bars, conflicting axis descriptions, and inconsistent base-2/base-4 formulas between revised B-tree statements and dynamic proofs.
